newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina, South Korea sign trade agreements.
newsitem.headline: Argentina, South Korea sign trade agreements.

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam signed Monday trade agreements with his Argentine counterpart Carlos Menem as a part of a "sales diplomacy" trip to Latin America.
Kim, who has already visited Guatemala and Chile and will travel also to Brazil and Peru, urged Korean and Argentine businessmen to "join forces to open an era of cooperation."
"Argentina is the key to enter the Mercosur," Menem said referring to the customs union formed by Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay.
Menem and Kim, who is travelling accompanied by 40 top Korean business leaders, spoke at a lunch after signing the deals on nuclear energy and air transport. No details were immediately available.
The Argentine Foreign Ministry called the visit the most important Korean economic mission ever to visit Argentina.
During his 24 hour stay Kim was seeking to boost South Korea's industrial competitiveness through the opening of new markets and facilitate the access of Argentine businesses to South Korean markets.
South Korea has reduced in 1995 its trade deficit with Argentina to $229 million from $457 million in 1994 and $479 million en 1993.
Kim will leave Tuesday for Brazil, the final leg of his 12 day tour.
